name: Bomdila
description: District headquarters of West Kameng at about 2,415 m elevation. Scenic hill station with apple orchards, Buddhist monasteries, viewpoints of Himalayan ranges, and a craft centre. Important stop on the Tezpur-Tawang highway.

name: Tawang Monastery (Gaden Namgyal Lhatse)
description: India’s largest Buddhist monastery and the second-largest in the world, founded in 1681 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso. Houses a 28-foot gilded Buddha statue, ancient manuscripts, and is the spiritual heart of the Monpa community in Tawang district.
facts: Birthplace region of the 6th Dalai Lama
Museum and library with rare texts

name: Tawang Town
description: District headquarters and main town of Tawang at about 3,000 m elevation, nestled in the Tawang Chu valley. Gateway for the monastery circuit, lakes, and high-altitude border areas, with markets, craft centres, and Monpa cultural base.
facts: Base for all major Tawang attractions

name: Sela Pass
description: High-altitude mountain pass at 4,170 m on the border of Tawang and West Kameng districts. Scenic gateway with Sela Lake, prayer flags, and dramatic Himalayan views; now bypassed by the all-weather Sela Tunnel.
facts: Sela Tunnel opened 2024 for year-round access

name: Nuranang Falls (Jang Falls)
description: Spectacular 100-metre-high waterfall near Jang town on the way to Tawang, cascading from Sela Pass slopes into a turquoise pool amid alpine scenery. Popular stop with a small hydel unit nearby.
facts: Near Jang, between Sela Pass and Tawang
Named after Nura from 1962 war legend

name: Sangetsar Tso (Madhuri Lake)
description: High-altitude lake at about 3,708 m on the road to Bum La, formed by an earthquake with submerged tree trunks rising from the water. Popularly called Madhuri Lake after a Bollywood film shoot; dramatic mountain backdrop.
facts: Requires army permission for Bum La road

name: Bum La Pass
description: High border pass at 4,600 m on the India–China Line of Actual Control, about 37 km from Tawang. Historic trade route and 1962 war site; offers stark high-altitude landscapes. Special army permit required.
facts: Indian nationals only with special permit

name: Urgelling Monastery
description: Historic Nyingma monastery founded in 1489, located a few kilometres from Tawang town. Birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama, Tsangyang Gyatso, in 1683. Smaller and quieter than the main Tawang Monastery.

name: Tawang War Memorial
description: Memorial in the form of a Buddhist stupa (Namgyal Chorten) near Tawang town honouring the 2,420 Indian soldiers who died in the 1962 Sino-Indian War. Features engraved names, gardens, and daily bugle ceremony.

name: Jaswant Garh Memorial
description: Army memorial near Nuranang on the Sela–Tawang road dedicated to Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat of 4 Garhwal Rifles, who held his post for 72 hours during the 1962 Battle of Nuranang and was awarded the Maha Vir Chakra posthumously.
facts: Honours Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat, MVC
About 25 km from Tawang on NH-13

name: Pankang Teng Tso (PT Tso)
description: High-altitude glacial lake about 17 km from Tawang on the Bum La road, surrounded by rhododendron slopes and snow peaks. Sacred to local Monpa people; often frozen in winter with mirror-like reflections.
